hypothesis: A callback/reblocking input path can preserve PortAudio inputBufferAdcTime and show whether complete 25 ms ADC frames reach the workspace within the 30 ms operational deadline, independent of blocking-read call jitter.

implementation.callback_contract: copy callback buffers with inputBufferAdcTime, reblock them into exact 400-sample frames, and compare ADC frame onset/end with Pa_GetStreamTime at workspace decision

interpretation_rules: ADC frame onset-to-decision includes the 25 ms frame accumulation interval; frame end-to-decision is the operational response latency.
PortAudio inputBufferAdcTime is a backend-provided ADC timestamp, but XMOS internal DSP delay remains outside the measurement.
Blocking capture-call deadline metrics remain diagnostic and cannot override or substitute the device-timestamped criterion.
All frames are expected to be quiet-path unless the environment naturally crosses the frozen saliency gate; no salient-workload claim is allowed otherwise.
promotion_boundary: Passing closes the device-timestamped quiet-path latency requirement only. Salient live workload timing, XMOS internal latency, and energy remain open.
